simple.meaning: לָפַת (lâphath) is a Hebrew word meaning “properly, to bend , i.e. (by implication) to clasp ; also (reflexively) to turn around or aside.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: לָפַת (H3943) appears 3 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Judges 16:29, with occurrences in Judges, Ruth, Job.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to לָפַת (H3943) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in לָפַת (H3943) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: לָפַת (lâphath) / H3943 is traced through Judges 16:29, Ruth 3:8, Job 6:18 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.short: properly, to bend , i.e. (by implication) to clasp ; also (reflexively) to turn around or aside
definitions.full: H3943. laphath [ לָפַת ] verb twist, turn, grasp with a twisting motion (Arabic twist, wring ; Assyrian lapâtu , overthrow , Dl HWB 382 ); — Qal Imperfect וַיִּלְמֹּת Judg 16:29 followed by accusative, Samson grasped the two middle columns. Niph`al Imperfect 3masculine singular וַיִּלָּפֵת Ruth 3:8 the man started up and twisted himself ; 3 masculine plural יִלָּֽפְתוּ Job 6:18 the paths of their way [i.e. of the streams] turn aside (twist, wind , with lessening force), so AV Hi De Da Bu > Ew Ol Di Siegf Du, who read Qal יִלְמְּתוּ or Pi`el יְלַמְּתוּ , making ארחות , = caravans , subject לָצוֺן לֵץ, see below ליץ .

occurrences.englishText: Samson took hold of the two middle pillars on which the house rested and leaned on them, the one with his right hand and the other with his left.
At midnight, the man was startled and turned himself; and behold, a woman lay at his feet.
The caravans that travel beside them turn away.
